label: input token m during the original phase
explanation: Token detector for the letter m in the original (pre-<DEL>) phase. It fires on 55% of all m inputs, with precision 1.0 and recall 0.985 on dev for original-phase m. It works at every position and every sequence length L, and does not depend on neighbouring tokens. It essentially never fires on other tokens (15 b and 2 x activations out of about 6M non-m steps). It is silent on the delimiter and nearly silent in the copy phase: copy-phase activations are 0.3% of mass, are weak (about 0.17 relative), and occur mostly when m is fed back as an input. Requiring the first occurrence of m (in_first) lowers recall to 0.89, so repeated m also fire. In the examples, the strongest activations (about 1.0 of max) are on m at the last original position, and the second m in a sequence is often somewhat weaker. These magnitude trends were seen in the examples but not systematically quantified.

issues: Test split: predicate has 0 false positives. All 1568 misses are in the copy phase and hold 0.3% of activation mass. They follow one pattern: m fed back as input at the first copy input step (recall_idx 1, where orig(0)=m), with weak activation of about 0.14-0.19 of max. This is a minor systematic tail and the explanation already describes it.

The copy phase is not 'mostly when m is fed back' in general. (phase==2)&(in_tok==m) has precision of only 0.017 on test, so m fed back fires almost only when it is the first fed-back token (recall_idx 1). This is a small imprecision in wording.

The magnitude claims match the top examples (the strongest are m at the last original position) but are not sharp. m at orig_idx L-1 covers only 15% of mass, and m at position 0 also reaches about 0.88 of max. The explanation correctly flags these trends as unchecked.
The rate is flat across orig_idx (0.033) and L (0.017 overall), and the delimiter step has zero activity. This confirms the claims of position and length independence and of silence on the delimiter.
